ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

schatzker — pattern 2

A 56-year-old woman falls onto a loaded knee. CT demonstrates both a lateral cortical split and a depressed segment of the lateral articular surface. The medial plateau is intact, and the metaphysis remains connected to the tibial shaft. Which Schatzker type best matches the CT description?

  1. Type V
  2. Type VI
  3. Type II
  4. Type III
  5. Type IV
Answer and explanation

Type II

Type II: A lateral plateau split combined with articular depression.

Option explanations

Type II: Type II: A lateral plateau split combined with articular depression.

Type III: Type III describes a pure depression of the lateral plateau without a lateral cortical split. The case instead matches Type II.

Type IV: Type IV describes a fracture involving the medial tibial plateau. The case instead matches Type II.

Type V: Type V describes a bicondylar tibial plateau fracture without complete metaphyseal-diaphyseal dissociation. The case instead matches Type II.

Type VI: Type VI describes a plateau fracture with metaphyseal-diaphyseal dissociation. The case instead matches Type II.
